text:
Samir: Anyone else seen weird provisional charges when a client disconnects right after a streaming EOF? Repro on prod: user opens stream, gets last chunk, client ack lost, reconnect -> we show provisional tokens then later they disappear but billing shows a spike :confused:
Ellie: can you paste the logs/snippet? Did this happen after the last router fix? :eyes:
Samir: here's the minimal trace (sanitized):
```
2026-03-23T15:02:11Z stream_open session=abc123 route=eu-west
2026-03-23T15:02:14Z token_emit prefix=204 suffix=32 provisional=true
2026-03-23T15:02:15Z client_disconnect code=1006
2026-03-23T15:02:16Z reconnect session=def456 route=us-east fallback=true
2026-03-23T15:02:20Z ledger_commit prefix=204 suffix=0 confirmed=true
```
Samir: note the suffix tokens show provisional=true earlier and then disappear on confirmed commit. But billing metrics had a short spike matching the provisional amount.
Pranav: hypothesis: heartbeat cutoff + cross-region handoff causes the provisional ledger to be emitted to billing subsystem before final confirmation. Routing fallback might emit a provisional escrow record that the billing path samples.
Ellie: hmm. Is this tied to toolcall truncation or just pure streaming tokens?
Samir: pure streaming in this case, no toolcalls. Also happened when client didn't send final ACK due to network flakiness.
Pranav: probably race between snapshot GC and provisional aggregation. If snapshot GC publishes pending tokens to the event bus before dedupe, billing consumer can see them and attribute. We saw similar once with prefetch sidecar spikes.
Ava (billing): Ava-bot FYI — I can correlate the spike to ingestion timestamps if you give me the 15:02-15:04 window. Billing consumer marks provisional events with header X-Provisional:1 but some consumers ignore it today.
Ellie: can we make the console surface a provisional/confirmed split in the per-route token waterfall? Right now it only shows a single "tokens" number which is confusing ops. :+1:
Samir: agree. Short-term I can add a graph to the route dashboard showing provisional vs confirmed for last 1h. Long-term we should prevent provisional events from hitting billing ingestion unless routed through the finalizer.
Pranav: also need to decide whether fallback routing should hold provisional tokens in the originating region until final commit. That adds latency but prevents double-observe. Maybe a soft hold policy behind a feature flag.
Ellie: UX question: if we add provisional toggles, will customers panic seeing higher transient numbers? Need a tooltip explaining provisional semantics and a reconciliation line.
Samir: SGTM. I'll spike a change: add provisional series + reconciliation delta in console, and patch router to avoid publishing provisional to the global billing bus until commit if feature flag on.
Pranav: ping me when you have the reproducer steps, I'll help test the hold strategy on canary.
Samir: repro + patch plan in a gist in ~2h. tagging @infra-bot for canary rollout when ready. :rocket:
infra-bot: deploy triggered for canary 'provisional-hold' -> build 2026.03.23.17, env=canary, owner=samir
Ava (billing): once you have the canary, send me the ingestion logs so I can confirm billing consumer ignores provisional header. I'll also add a dashboard panel for transient spikes.
Ellie: thanks — this should address a bunch of "why did we bill then not bill" tickets. :relieved:
